source_caption:
George R.R. Martin deliberately designed Jaime Lannister as a brilliant, devastating subversion of the traditional fantasy “Prince Charming” trope. Nikolaj Coster-Waldau masterfully navigates one of television’s most complex psychological arcs, taking a character introduced as an arrogant, incestuous child-murderer and slowly dismantling his entire identity. By permanently stripping away his legendary sword hand—the singular physical attribute that defined his immense ego and worldly value—the series brilliantly forces the audience to grapple with a profound, uncomfortable question: can a man entirely defined by his most monstrous acts ever truly earn redemption?
⠀
Game of Thrones (2011), created by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss, starring Peter Dinklage, Lena Headey, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau. Nine noble families wage a bloody, ruthless, and politically complex war for total control over the mythical land of Westeros, while an ancient, terrifying supernatural force slowly awakens in the frozen north.

source_details.synopsis: Game of Thrones is an American fantasy drama television series created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss for HBO. It is the first adaptation of A Song of Ice and Fire, a series of high fantasy novels by George R. R. Martin, and the first in what would become the Game of Thrones franchise. The show premiered on HBO in the United States on April 17, 2011, and concluded on May 19, 2019, with 73 episodes broadcast over eight seasons. Set on the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos, Game of Thrones has a large ensemble cast and follows several story arcs throughout the course of the show.
